title: New DHCP Server Authorized in Active Directory
description: A DHCP server was newly authorized in Active Directory, permitting it to begin leasing addresses to clients on the network. Since an authorized rogue DHCP server can redirect DNS, gateway, and routing for every client that leases from it, unexpected authorization is a high-value early-warning signal.

data_sources.name: AD Directory Service Changes
data_sources.description: Authorization object creation under CN=NetServices.

detection_logic: Filters AD audit events for DHCP server authorization object creation.
spl:
index=<ad_index> sourcetype=<ad_audit_sourcetype> object_class="dHCPClass" action="created"
| table _time, user, server_ip, server_name
tuning_guidance: Very low expected volume outside planned infrastructure changes; alert on all occurrences.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification against a change ticket.
Verify the server is on the approved DHCP infrastructure inventory.
response_guidance: Deauthorize immediately if unconfirmed and investigate the authorizing account for broader AD compromise.
author: Threat Detection Library
attack_mapping_note: ATT&CK has no dedicated technique for AD-based DHCP server authorization; T1584.008 (Compromise Infrastructure: Network Devices) is used as the closest-fit technique since authorization is the step that turns a server into trusted network infrastructure.

title: DHCP Server Authorization Removed
description: A previously authorized DHCP server had its AD authorization removed, which will cause it to stop leasing addresses (Windows DHCP servers self-disable when they detect they are unauthorized). This can be a legitimate decommission or a denial-of-service action.

data_sources.name: AD Directory Service Changes
data_sources.description: Authorization object deletion.

detection_logic: Filters AD audit events for DHCP authorization object deletion.
spl:
index=<ad_index> sourcetype=<ad_audit_sourcetype> object_class="dHCPClass" action="deleted"
| table _time, user, server_ip, server_name
tuning_guidance: Confirm against decommission tickets; unticketed removal on a production server is an availability incident.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification.
Check whether the server is still expected to be serving leases.
response_guidance: Re-authorize immediately if unauthorized removal caused a service outage.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: DHCP Server Authorized by Unusual Administrator
description: A DHCP server authorization was performed by an account outside the small, expected set of administrators who normally handle DHCP infrastructure provisioning.

data_sources.name: AD Directory Service Changes
data_sources.description: Authorization events joined against an expected-operator lookup.

detection_logic: Joins DHCP authorization events against a lookup of expected DHCP administrators.
spl:
index=<ad_index> sourcetype=<ad_audit_sourcetype> object_class="dHCPClass" action="created"
| lookup dhcp_admins.csv user OUTPUT is_expected
| where isnull(is_expected)
| table _time, user, server_ip
tuning_guidance: Maintain the expected-DHCP-admin lookup; small, stable list in most environments.
investigation_steps: Confirm the account's role and business justification.
response_guidance: Deauthorize if unconfirmed and investigate the account.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: DHCP Server Authorized from Unusual Management Host
description: The authorization action originated from a management workstation/host outside the expected set of DHCP/AD administration hosts.

data_sources.name: AD Directory Service Changes
data_sources.description: Authorization events with source host, joined against an expected-management-host lookup.

detection_logic: Joins authorization events against a lookup of expected management hosts.
spl:
index=<ad_index> sourcetype=<ad_audit_sourcetype> object_class="dHCPClass" action="created"
| lookup dhcp_mgmt_hosts.csv src_host OUTPUT is_expected
| where isnull(is_expected)
| table _time, user, src_host, server_ip
tuning_guidance: Maintain the expected-management-host lookup.
investigation_steps: Confirm the source host is an approved administration workstation.
response_guidance: Investigate if unconfirmed; deauthorize pending verification.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Multiple DHCP Servers Authorized in Short Period
description: More than one DHCP server was authorized within a short window, which is unusual outside a planned infrastructure rollout and could indicate an attacker staging multiple rogue servers or rapidly re-authorizing after being blocked.

data_sources.name: AD Directory Service Changes
data_sources.description: Authorization event count in a rolling window.

detection_logic: Counts distinct DHCP authorization events in a rolling window.
spl:
index=<ad_index> sourcetype=<ad_audit_sourcetype> object_class="dHCPClass" action="created"
| bin _time span=1h
| stats dc(server_ip) as new_servers, values(server_ip) as servers by _time user
| where new_servers>=2
tuning_guidance: Expected during planned multi-server rollouts; require a change ticket for anything else.
investigation_steps: Confirm against a change ticket for planned infrastructure expansion.
response_guidance: Deauthorize unconfirmed servers immediately.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Rogue Server Attempting to Operate Without Authorization
description: A DHCP server detected another DHCP server on the network operating without AD authorization (Windows DHCP servers periodically check for and log this). This is direct evidence of a rogue server attempting to serve leases.

data_sources.name: DHCP Server Operational Log
data_sources.description: Unauthorized-server-detected events.

detection_logic: Filters the DHCP Server Operational channel for unauthorized-server-detected events.
spl:
index=<windows_index> sourcetype="WinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-DHCP-Server/Operational" EventCode=1046
| table _time, host, rogue_server_ip
tuning_guidance: Very low expected volume; alert on all occurrences.
investigation_steps: Physically or via network telemetry locate the rogue server.
Correlate with DHCP-NET-### rogue-server network detections.
response_guidance: Isolate the rogue server from the network immediately.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Previously Trusted DHCP Server Loses Authorization Unexpectedly
description: A production DHCP server that has been authorized and serving leases for an extended period loses its authorization outside a planned maintenance window, which will stop it from issuing new leases and can be a denial-of-service action against network onboarding.

data_sources.name: AD Directory Service Changes + DHCP Operational Log
data_sources.path: Authorization removal joined against a long-lived-server baseline
data_sources.description: Distinguishes new/short-lived servers from established production servers.

detection_logic: Filters authorization-removed events for servers present in a long-lived-server baseline lookup.
spl:
index=<ad_index> sourcetype=<ad_audit_sourcetype> object_class="dHCPClass" action="deleted"
| lookup established_dhcp_servers.csv server_ip OUTPUT first_authorized
| where isnotnull(first_authorized)
| table _time, user, server_ip, first_authorized
tuning_guidance: Maintain the established-server baseline lookup; require a change ticket for planned removal.
investigation_steps: Confirm against a change ticket.
Assess client-onboarding impact immediately.
response_guidance: Re-authorize immediately if unauthorized and investigate the removing account.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Privileged AD Change Immediately Followed by DHCP Authorization
description: A privileged AD change (e.g. the acting account was granted Enterprise Admin or added to a group with DHCP-administration delegation) is immediately followed by that same account authorizing a new DHCP server — consistent with an attacker escalating privilege specifically to stand up a rogue DHCP server.

data_sources.name: AD Directory Service Changes
data_sources.path: Privilege-grant events joined with subsequent DHCP authorization events for the same account
data_sources.description: Sequence correlation.

detection_logic: Sequences a privilege-grant event with a subsequent DHCP authorization event for the same account within a bounded window.
spl:
index=<ad_index> sourcetype=<ad_audit_sourcetype> (EventCode=4728 OR EventCode=4732 OR EventCode=4756) OR (object_class="dHCPClass" action="created")
| eval stage=case(object_class="dHCPClass","2_authorize", true(),"1_privilege_grant")
| transaction user maxspan=1h startswith=eval(stage="1_privilege_grant") endswith=eval(stage="2_authorize")
| table _time, user, eventcount
tuning_guidance: Very low expected false-positive rate; treat every confirmed instance as a live incident.
investigation_steps: Treat as a confirmed privilege-escalation-to-rogue-infrastructure incident.
Deauthorize the server and revert the privilege grant immediately.
response_guidance: Full incident response: suspend the account, deauthorize the server, and audit all AD activity by the account.
author: Threat Detection Library

threshold.baseline_condition: privileged AD change -> DHCP server authorization, same account

title: DHCP Administrators Security Group Membership Changed
description: Membership in the DHCP Administrators (or equivalent delegated) security group changed, expanding or altering who can authorize servers, modify scopes, and change DHCP options across the environment.

data_sources.name: AD Group Membership Changes
data_sources.path: Security group membership change events for DHCP-administrative groups
data_sources.description: Group membership add/remove events.

detection_logic: Filters AD group membership change events for the DHCP administrative group(s).
spl:
index=<ad_index> sourcetype=<ad_audit_sourcetype> EventCode IN (4728,4729,4732,4733) group_name="DHCP Administrators"
| table _time, user, target_user, group_name, EventCode
tuning_guidance: Low volume; alert on all occurrences outside a documented onboarding/offboarding process.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification with the requesting manager.
response_guidance: Revert if unauthorized and audit the added account's subsequent DHCP activity.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: DHCP Server Service Stopped
description: The Windows DHCP Server service (DHCPServer) stopped, which will halt lease issuance for every scope on this server until it restarts.

data_sources.name: System Event Log
data_sources.description: Service Control Manager stop events for the DHCP Server service.

detection_logic: Filters the System log for Service Control Manager events indicating the DHCP Server service stopped.
spl:
index=<windows_index> sourcetype="WinEventLog:System" EventCode=7036 service_name="DHCP Server" state="stopped"
| table _time, host, user
tuning_guidance: Correlate with maintenance windows; unticketed stops on production servers are an availability incident.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification.
Assess lease-issuance impact on affected scopes.
response_guidance: Restart the service and investigate the stopping account/process if unconfirmed.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: DHCP Server Service Restarted Unexpectedly
description: The DHCP Server service restarted outside a declared maintenance window, which can be operational instability or a symptom of an attacker forcing a reload after a configuration/binary tamper.

data_sources.name: System Event Log
data_sources.description: Service start events joined against a maintenance-window lookup.

detection_logic: Filters service-start events for the DHCP Server service where a maintenance-window lookup does not cover the event time.
spl:
index=<windows_index> sourcetype="WinEventLog:System" EventCode=7036 service_name="DHCP Server" state="running"
| lookup maintenance_windows.csv host, _time OUTPUT in_window
| where isnull(in_window) OR in_window=0
| table _time, host
tuning_guidance: Requires a maintained maintenance-window lookup.
investigation_steps: Check for a preceding configuration or binary-path change.
Review System log for crash events immediately prior.
response_guidance: Investigate if unconfirmed and unexplained by a crash.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Repeated DHCP Server Service Crashes
description: The DHCP Server service crashed and restarted multiple times in a short window, which can indicate an exploitation attempt against the service, a malformed-packet attack, or a resource-exhaustion condition.

data_sources.name: System/Application Event Log
data_sources.description: Service crash/unexpected-termination events.

detection_logic: Counts unexpected DHCP Server service termination events per host in a rolling window.
spl:
index=<windows_index> sourcetype IN ("WinEventLog:System","WinEventLog:Application") EventCode=7031 service_name="DHCP Server"
| bin _time span=1h
| stats count as crashes by host, _time
| where crashes>=3
tuning_guidance: Very low expected false-positive rate; investigate every occurrence.
investigation_steps: Review crash dump/Application log for the fault module.
Check for concurrent network anomalies (starvation, malformed packets) on this server.
response_guidance: Treat as a potential exploitation attempt against the DHCP service pending root-cause analysis.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: DHCP Server Service Startup Type Changed
description: The DHCP Server service's startup type was changed (e.g. Automatic to Disabled/Manual), which controls whether it comes back after a reboot.

data_sources.name: System/Security Event Log
data_sources.description: Service configuration change events.

detection_logic: Filters service-configuration-change events for the DHCP Server service's start type.
spl:
index=<windows_index> sourcetype="WinEventLog:System" EventCode=7040 service_name="DHCP Server"
| table _time, host, user, new_start_type
tuning_guidance: Low volume; alert on all occurrences on production servers.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification.
response_guidance: Revert to Automatic if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: DHCP Server Service Account Changed
description: The account the DHCP Server service runs as was changed, which is unusual since the service normally runs as Local System / Network Service and could indicate an attacker configuring it to run under a compromised privileged account for persistence.

data_sources.name: System Event Log
data_sources.description: Service configuration change events with the LogOnAs field.

detection_logic: Filters service-configuration-change events for the DHCP Server service's logon account.
spl:
index=<windows_index> sourcetype="WinEventLog:System" EventCode=7040 service_name="DHCP Server" field_changed="LogOnAs"
| table _time, host, user, new_logon_account
tuning_guidance: Very low expected volume; alert on all occurrences.
investigation_steps: Verify the new account and its privilege level.
Treat as a likely persistence attempt if the new account is unexpectedly privileged.
response_guidance: Revert to the default service account immediately if unauthorized.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1543: Create or Modify System Process

author: Threat Detection Library

title: DHCP Server Service Binary Path Changed
description: The DHCP Server service's binary path was changed, which is a classic service-hijacking persistence technique — the next service start will execute the attacker-specified binary with the service's privileges (typically SYSTEM).

data_sources.name: System Event Log
data_sources.description: Service configuration change events with the ImagePath field.

detection_logic: Filters service-configuration-change events for the DHCP Server service's binary path.
spl:
index=<windows_index> sourcetype="WinEventLog:System" EventCode=7040 service_name="DHCP Server" field_changed="ImagePath"
| table _time, host, user, new_binary_path
tuning_guidance: Alert on every occurrence; there is no legitimate reason to change this on a standard installation.
investigation_steps: Treat as a live incident.
Do not allow the service to restart until the binary path is verified/reverted.
response_guidance: Revert to the original binary path immediately and treat the host as compromised pending investigation.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1543: Create or Modify System Process

author: Threat Detection Library

title: DHCP Server Service Permissions Changed
description: The Windows service ACL (Security Descriptor) for the DHCP Server service was modified, potentially granting a non-administrative account rights to reconfigure or restart the service — a common precursor to service-binary-hijack persistence.

data_sources.name: Security Event Log
data_sources.description: Service DACL modification events.

detection_logic: Filters Security log events for service security-descriptor changes on the DHCP Server service.
spl:
index=<windows_index> sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=4670 object_name="DHCPServer"
| table _time, host, user
tuning_guidance: Very low expected volume; alert on all occurrences.
investigation_steps: Review the new ACL for unexpected grantees.
Cross-reference with DHCP-006 for a subsequent binary-path change.
response_guidance: Revert to default permissions if unauthorized.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1222: File and Directory Permissions Modification

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Configuration Change Immediately Followed by DHCP Service Restart
description: A service-level configuration change (binary path, logon account, or permissions) was immediately followed by the DHCP Server service restarting, consistent with an attacker completing a service-hijack persistence chain and forcing their payload to execute.

data_sources.name: System/Security Event Log
data_sources.path: Service configuration change joined with a subsequent service start event
data_sources.description: Sequence correlation.

detection_logic: Sequences a service-configuration-change event with a subsequent service-start event for the DHCP Server service within a bounded window.
spl:
index=<windows_index> sourcetype="WinEventLog:System" service_name="DHCP Server" (EventCode=7040 OR EventCode=7036)
| eval stage=case(EventCode=7040,"1_config", EventCode=7036 AND state="running","2_restart", true(), null())
| where isnotnull(stage)
| transaction host maxspan=10m startswith=eval(stage="1_config") endswith=eval(stage="2_restart")
| table _time, host, user, eventcount
tuning_guidance: Very low expected false-positive rate; treat as a live incident.
investigation_steps: Assume the service is now running attacker-controlled code.
Isolate the host immediately.
response_guidance: Isolate and investigate as an active compromise; do not simply revert the configuration without full forensic review.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1543: Create or Modify System Process

author: Threat Detection Library

threshold.baseline_condition: service config change -> service restart, same host

title: DHCP Audit Logging Disabled
description: DHCP audit logging was disabled on the server, which removes the primary telemetry source this entire catalogue depends on. There is essentially no routine reason to disable it on a production server.

data_sources.name: DHCP Server Admin Log
data_sources.description: Audit-logging-disabled configuration events.

detection_logic: Filters the DHCP Server Admin channel for audit-logging-disabled events.
spl:
index=<windows_index> sourcetype="WinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-DHCP-Server/Admin" EventCode=1042
| table _time, host, user
tuning_guidance: Alert on every occurrence; exception-list only via a confirmed change ticket.
investigation_steps: Treat as a live incident.
Immediately check for other suspicious DHCP activity in the period before this event, since this is very likely a cover-up.
response_guidance: Re-enable audit logging immediately and treat the server as compromised pending investigation.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: DHCP Audit Log Path Changed
description: The directory where DHCP audit logs are written was changed, which could redirect logging to a location that is not being collected/forwarded, silently blinding SIEM visibility while logging technically continues.

data_sources.name: DHCP Server Admin Log
data_sources.description: Audit log path configuration change events.

detection_logic: Filters audit-log-path configuration change events.
spl:
index=<windows_index> sourcetype="WinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-DHCP-Server/Admin" EventCode=1042 setting="AuditLogPath"
| table _time, host, user, new_path
tuning_guidance: Very low expected volume; alert on all occurrences.
investigation_steps: Verify the new path is still covered by log collection.
Confirm business justification.
response_guidance: Revert and verify collection resumes.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: DHCP Audit Log Retention/Disk-Check Interval Changed
description: The DHCP audit log's disk-check/rollover configuration was changed, which can shorten the effective on-disk retention of audit history.

data_sources.name: DHCP Server Admin Log
data_sources.description: Audit-log retention/disk-check configuration change events.

detection_logic: Filters audit-log retention configuration change events.
spl:
index=<windows_index> sourcetype="WinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-DHCP-Server/Admin" EventCode=1042 setting="DiskCheckInterval"
| table _time, host, user
tuning_guidance: Low volume; alert on all occurrences.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification.
response_guidance: Revert if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: DHCP Audit Log File Deleted
description: A DHCP audit log file was deleted from disk, directly destroying local forensic history for the period it covered.

data_sources.name: Security Event Log
data_sources.path: Security (file-system auditing on the DHCP log directory)
data_sources.description: File deletion events in the DHCP audit log directory.

detection_logic: Filters file-deletion events (Security 4660/4663 with an accompanying handle-close) scoped to the DHCP audit log directory.
spl:
index=<windows_index> sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode IN (4660,4663) object_name="*\\DHCP\\*.log"
| table _time, host, user, object_name
tuning_guidance: Requires file-system SACL auditing enabled on the DHCP log directory; alert on all occurrences.
investigation_steps: Treat as a live incident.
Check for a backup/forwarded copy of the deleted log to reconstruct recent activity.
response_guidance: Treat the server as compromised pending investigation.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: DHCP Audit Log Directory Permissions Changed
description: File-system permissions on the DHCP audit log directory were changed, potentially allowing a non-administrative account to delete or tamper with log files, or restricting the account used for log collection.

data_sources.name: Security Event Log
data_sources.description: DACL modification events on the DHCP log directory.

detection_logic: Filters DACL modification events scoped to the DHCP audit log directory.
spl:
index=<windows_index> sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=4670 object_name="*\\DHCP\\*"
| table _time, host, user
tuning_guidance: Requires SACL auditing on the directory; low expected volume.
investigation_steps: Review the new ACL for unexpected grantees or removed collection-account access.
response_guidance: Revert to default permissions if unauthorized.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1222: File and Directory Permissions Modification

author: Threat Detection Library

title: DHCP Logging Configuration Weakened
description: A DHCP logging-related configuration setting was changed to a less-verbose or less-durable state (e.g. reduced max log size, disabled Yes/No prompt for actions logged).

data_sources.name: DHCP Server Admin Log
data_sources.description: Logging-related configuration change events.

detection_logic: Filters DHCP configuration change events for logging-related settings moving to a weaker value.
spl:
index=<windows_index> sourcetype="WinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-DHCP-Server/Admin" EventCode=1042 setting="MaxLogFilesSize"
| where new_value < old_value
| table _time, host, user, old_value, new_value
tuning_guidance: Correlate with a legitimate disk-space-management change ticket before escalating.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification.
response_guidance: Revert if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Unexpected Gap in DHCP Audit Logging
description: A DHCP server that normally forwards a baseline volume of audit events has produced none for longer than its expected heartbeat interval, while other telemetry (e.g. System log heartbeats, ping/health checks) shows the server is still up — consistent with audit logging having been silently disabled or the forwarding pipeline broken.

data_sources.name: DHCP audit log (fleet-aggregated)
data_sources.path: Server inventory joined against last-seen DHCP audit event time
data_sources.description: Detects the absence of expected telemetry, not a specific event.

detection_logic: Compares each known DHCP server's last audit-log event time against an expected heartbeat interval derived from its historical baseline.
spl:
| tstats latest(_time) as last_seen where index=<dhcp_index> by host
| eval gap_hours=round((now()-last_seen)/3600,1)
| where gap_hours > 6
| table host, last_seen, gap_hours
tuning_guidance: Tune the gap threshold to the fleet's actual expected event cadence; servers under planned maintenance should be suppressed via a maintenance lookup.
investigation_steps: Verify the server is still running and network-reachable.
Check for DHCP-AUD-001 (logging disabled) or a forwarding-pipeline failure as the cause.
response_guidance: Escalate unexplained gaps as a probable anti-forensics indicator.
author: Threat Detection Library

threshold.baseline_condition: no DHCP audit events received from a previously-active server

title: DHCP Activity Continues While Audit Telemetry Disappears
description: Client lease activity (visible via a secondary source such as DNS dynamic-update records or network telemetry) continues on a server whose DHCP audit-log stream has gone silent, proving the server is still operating while its own audit trail has been suppressed — the clearest possible confirmation of DHCP-AUD-007's gap detection.

data_sources.name: DHCP audit log + DNS dynamic update log
data_sources.path: Cross-source comparison: DHCP audit silence vs. continued DNS updates attributable to the same server
data_sources.description: Requires a secondary corroborating telemetry source.

detection_logic: Correlates a DHCP audit-log gap (DHCP-AUD-007) with continued DNS dynamic-update activity attributable to the same DHCP server.
spl:
| tstats latest(_time) as last_dhcp_seen where index=<dhcp_index> by host
| eval gap_hours=round((now()-last_dhcp_seen)/3600,1)
| where gap_hours > 6
| join type=inner host [
    | tstats count as dns_updates where index=<dns_index> sourcetype=<dns_dynamic_update_sourcetype> earliest=-6h by dhcp_source_host
    | rename dhcp_source_host as host
  ]
| where dns_updates > 0
| table host, last_dhcp_seen, gap_hours, dns_updates
tuning_guidance: Very low expected false-positive rate given the cross-source corroboration; treat as a confirmed incident.
investigation_steps: Treat as a confirmed active anti-forensics incident.
Assume the server is compromised and every lease issued during the gap is unverified.
response_guidance: Isolate the server and begin full forensic investigation; do not simply re-enable logging and move on.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: DHCP Audit Log Restored to Different (Weaker) Configuration After Incident
description: Audit logging was re-enabled after having been disabled, but with a weaker configuration than before (e.g. shorter retention, reduced max size), suggesting an attempt to appear compliant while continuing to limit forensic visibility.

data_sources.name: DHCP Server Admin Log
data_sources.description: Audit-logging re-enablement events compared against the pre-disablement configuration baseline.

detection_logic: Compares the configuration present when audit logging is re-enabled against a stored pre-disablement baseline.
spl:
index=<windows_index> sourcetype="WinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-DHCP-Server/Admin" EventCode=1042 setting="AuditLogEnabled" new_value="1"
| lookup dhcp_audit_config_baseline.csv host OUTPUT baseline_max_size, baseline_path
| where new_max_size < baseline_max_size OR new_path != baseline_path
| table _time, host, user, new_max_size, baseline_max_size
tuning_guidance: Requires a stored pre-incident configuration baseline; low volume once available.
investigation_steps: Restore full configuration and investigate why it was weakened.
response_guidance: Restore the original configuration.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: DHCP Scope Created
description: A new DHCP scope was created. Routine during planned network expansion; the building block for the higher-priority anomaly detections below.

data_sources.name: DHCP Audit Log
data_sources.description: Scope creation events.

detection_logic: Filters the DHCP audit log for scope-creation events.
spl:
index=<dhcp_index> action="scope created"
| table _time, host, user, scope, subnet
tuning_guidance: Not independently alertable at scale; feed into DHCP-011/012 rather than alerting on every occurrence.
investigation_steps: Correlate with change management.
response_guidance: No independent response.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: DHCP Scope Deleted
description: A DHCP scope was deleted, which will make its address range unavailable for lease and drop any active leases within it at their next renewal.

data_sources.name: DHCP Audit Log
data_sources.description: Scope deletion events.

detection_logic: Filters the DHCP audit log for scope-deletion events.
spl:
index=<dhcp_index> action="scope deleted"
| table _time, host, user, scope
tuning_guidance: Confirm against decommission tickets for production scopes.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification.
Assess client-onboarding impact.
response_guidance: Recreate if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Multiple DHCP Scopes Disabled at Once
description: Several DHCP scopes were disabled by the same account within a short window, which will halt lease issuance across all of them simultaneously — consistent with a destructive/ransomware-style attack against network-onboarding availability rather than routine single-scope maintenance.

data_sources.name: DHCP Audit Log
data_sources.description: Scope-disabled events, counted per account in a rolling window.

detection_logic: Counts scope-disabled events by the same account in a rolling window.
spl:
index=<dhcp_index> action="scope state changed" new_state="disabled"
| bin _time span=15m
| stats dc(scope) as disabled_scopes, values(scope) as scopes by _time user host
| where disabled_scopes>=3
tuning_guidance: Very low expected false-positive rate; treat as a live incident.
investigation_steps: Treat as a live incident.
Re-enable affected scopes immediately if unconfirmed.
Identify and suspend the acting account.
response_guidance: Full incident response: re-enable scopes, suspend the account, and audit all recent DHCP activity by it.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Bulk DHCP Scope Deletion
description: Several DHCP scopes were deleted by the same account within a short window — a strong destructive-attack indicator, since legitimate scope removal is normally spaced out and change-ticketed individually.

data_sources.name: DHCP Audit Log
data_sources.description: Scope-deletion events, counted per account in a rolling window.

detection_logic: Counts scope-deletion events by the same account in a rolling window.
spl:
index=<dhcp_index> action="scope deleted"
| bin _time span=15m
| stats dc(scope) as deleted_scopes, values(scope) as scopes by _time user host
| where deleted_scopes>=3
tuning_guidance: Very low expected false-positive rate; treat as a live incident.
investigation_steps: Treat as a live incident.
Identify and suspend the acting account.
Assess whether recreation from backup is possible.
response_guidance: Full incident response.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: New DHCP Scope Outside Approved Network Ranges
description: A new scope was created for a subnet range outside the organization's documented approved network allocations, which could indicate an attacker standing up address space to support a rogue segment or bypass IPAM controls.

data_sources.name: DHCP Audit Log
data_sources.description: Scope creation events joined against an approved-subnet-range lookup.

detection_logic: Joins scope-creation events against a lookup of approved network ranges (typically sourced from IPAM).
spl:
index=<dhcp_index> action="scope created"
| lookup approved_subnet_ranges.csv subnet OUTPUT is_approved
| where isnull(is_approved)
| table _time, host, user, scope, subnet
tuning_guidance: Requires a maintained IPAM-sourced approved-range lookup; high value once available.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification and update IPAM if legitimate.
response_guidance: Disable/delete if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: DHCP Scope Address Range Expanded into Another Subnet
description: A scope's start/end address range was widened to overlap with another subnet's allocated space, which can cause address conflicts and give the DHCP server authority to issue leases outside its intended segment.

data_sources.name: DHCP Audit Log
data_sources.description: Scope range-change events with old/new start and end addresses.

detection_logic: Compares old and new scope ranges and flags expansion beyond the scope's original subnet boundary.
spl:
index=<dhcp_index> action="scope range changed"
| eval expanded=if(new_start<old_start OR new_end>old_end, 1, 0)
| where expanded=1
| table _time, host, user, scope, old_start, old_end, new_start, new_end
tuning_guidance: Confirm against IPAM/change tickets for planned scope resizing.
investigation_steps: Verify the new range does not overlap an already-allocated subnet.
response_guidance: Revert if unauthorized or overlapping.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: DHCP Scope Created by Unusual Administrator
description: A scope was created by an account outside the expected set of DHCP administrators.

data_sources.name: DHCP Audit Log
data_sources.description: Scope creation events joined against an expected-operator lookup.

detection_logic: Joins scope-creation events against a lookup of expected DHCP administrators.
spl:
index=<dhcp_index> action="scope created"
| lookup dhcp_admins.csv user OUTPUT is_expected
| where isnull(is_expected)
| table _time, host, user, scope
tuning_guidance: Maintain the expected-DHCP-admin lookup.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification.
response_guidance: Investigate if unconfirmed.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Production DHCP Scope Disabled
description: A scope tagged as serving a production network was disabled, halting new lease issuance for that segment.

data_sources.name: DHCP Audit Log
data_sources.description: Scope-disabled events joined against a scope-criticality lookup.

detection_logic: Filters scope-disabled events where the scope is tagged production in a criticality lookup.
spl:
index=<dhcp_index> action="scope state changed" new_state="disabled"
| lookup scope_criticality.csv scope OUTPUT tier
| where tier="production"
| table _time, host, user, scope
tuning_guidance: Requires a maintained scope-criticality lookup.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification immediately.
response_guidance: Re-enable if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: DHCP Scope Recreated Shortly After Deletion
description: A scope was deleted and a scope covering the same or overlapping range was recreated shortly after, which can be a technique to reset scope-level history/statistics or an operational recovery — worth distinguishing via the acting accounts involved.

data_sources.name: DHCP Audit Log
data_sources.description: Scope deletion followed by scope creation for an overlapping subnet.

detection_logic: Sequences a scope-deletion event with a subsequent scope-creation event for the same subnet within a bounded window.
spl:
index=<dhcp_index> (action="scope deleted" OR action="scope created")
| eval stage=case(action="scope deleted","1_delete", action="scope created","2_create", true(), null())
| where isnotnull(stage)
| transaction subnet maxspan=1h startswith=eval(stage="1_delete") endswith=eval(stage="2_create")
| table _time, subnet, user, eventcount
tuning_guidance: Correlate with change tickets for planned scope rebuilds.
investigation_steps: Compare the recreated scope's reservations/options/exclusions against the pre-deletion baseline for unexpected differences.
response_guidance: Investigate if unconfirmed; verify the recreated scope's configuration matches expectations.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: DHCP Scope Lease Duration Drastically Changed
description: A scope's lease duration was changed by a large factor (much shorter or much longer than the previous value), which can affect renewal load, address-pool churn, or the window an attacker-controlled option value stays in effect.

data_sources.name: DHCP Audit Log
data_sources.description: Lease-duration configuration change events.

detection_logic: Compares old and new lease-time values and flags large relative changes.
spl:
index=<dhcp_index> action="scope lease time changed"
| eval ratio=new_lease_time/old_lease_time
| where ratio>=4 OR ratio<=0.25
| table _time, host, user, scope, old_lease_time, new_lease_time
tuning_guidance: Confirm against change tickets; large changes are sometimes legitimate DR/failover tuning.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification.
response_guidance: Revert if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: DHCP Scope Subnet Mask Changed
description: A scope's subnet mask was changed, which alters the effective network/broadcast boundary communicated to clients and can create routing or address-conflict issues.

data_sources.name: DHCP Audit Log
data_sources.description: Subnet mask configuration change events.

detection_logic: Filters subnet-mask configuration change events.
spl:
index=<dhcp_index> action="scope subnet mask changed"
| table _time, host, user, scope, old_mask, new_mask
tuning_guidance: Very low expected volume outside network redesign; alert on all occurrences on production scopes.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification against network design documentation.
response_guidance: Revert if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Same Administrator Modifying Many DHCP Scopes
description: A single account modifies an unusually high number of distinct scopes within a short window, which is atypical for routine per-scope maintenance and more consistent with a scripted attack or compromised automation credential making bulk changes.

data_sources.name: DHCP Audit Log
data_sources.description: Distinct-scope-modified count per account in a rolling window.

detection_logic: Counts distinct scopes modified by the same account in a rolling window.
spl:
index=<dhcp_index> action="scope*changed"
| bin _time span=1h
| stats dc(scope) as scopes_modified by _time user host
| where scopes_modified>=10
tuning_guidance: Tune out known bulk-configuration automation accounts.
investigation_steps: Identify the account and confirm against known automation tooling.
response_guidance: Investigate if not attributable to approved tooling.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: DHCP Exclusion Range Created
description: An exclusion range was added to a scope, removing those addresses from the leasable pool. Routine for reserving infrastructure addresses, but a large or unusual exclusion can also be used to starve legitimate clients or quietly reserve addresses for attacker infrastructure that will never be flagged as an active lease.

data_sources.name: DHCP Audit Log
data_sources.description: Exclusion range creation events.

detection_logic: Filters exclusion-range creation events.
spl:
index=<dhcp_index> action="exclusion range added"
| table _time, host, user, scope, excl_start, excl_end
tuning_guidance: Not independently alertable at scale; feed into DHCP-022/023 for size-based escalation.
investigation_steps: Correlate with change management.
response_guidance: No independent response.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Large DHCP Exclusion Range Added
description: An exclusion range covering an unusually large portion of a scope's address space was added, which can starve the scope of leasable addresses for legitimate clients — a subtler denial-of-service than an outright deletion.

data_sources.name: DHCP Audit Log
data_sources.description: Exclusion range size as a percentage of total scope size.

detection_logic: Computes exclusion range size as a percentage of the scope's total address space and flags large values.
spl:
index=<dhcp_index> action="exclusion range added"
| eval excl_size=excl_end_int-excl_start_int
| eval excl_size_pct=round((excl_size/scope_total_size)*100,1)
| where excl_size_pct>=25
| table _time, host, user, scope, excl_start, excl_end, excl_size_pct
tuning_guidance: Confirm against change tickets for legitimate large infrastructure reservations.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification.
Assess remaining leasable capacity for the scope.
response_guidance: Reduce/remove if unauthorized and address-exhaustion risk is confirmed.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1499.001: OS Exhaustion Flood

author: Threat Detection Library

title: DHCP Exclusion Removed, Freeing Previously Protected Addresses
description: An exclusion range was removed, making previously-protected addresses (often reserved for infrastructure) available for lease to arbitrary clients — potentially allowing an attacker's device to obtain an address that was intentionally kept out of the DHCP pool.

data_sources.name: DHCP Audit Log
data_sources.description: Exclusion range removal events.

detection_logic: Filters exclusion-range removal events.
spl:
index=<dhcp_index> action="exclusion range removed"
| table _time, host, user, scope, excl_start, excl_end
tuning_guidance: Confirm against change tickets.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification.
Monitor the freed range for the next lease issued.
response_guidance: Re-add the exclusion if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Exclusions Manipulated Across Many Scopes
description: Exclusion ranges were added or removed across an unusually high number of distinct scopes by the same account within a short window, consistent with a scripted fleet-wide attack aimed at broad address-pool disruption.

data_sources.name: DHCP Audit Log
data_sources.description: Distinct-scope exclusion-change count per account in a rolling window.

detection_logic: Counts distinct scopes with an exclusion change by the same account in a rolling window.
spl:
index=<dhcp_index> (action="exclusion range added" OR action="exclusion range removed")
| bin _time span=1h
| stats dc(scope) as scopes_affected by _time user
| where scopes_affected>=5
tuning_guidance: Tune out known bulk-configuration automation accounts.
investigation_steps: Identify the account and confirm against known automation tooling.
response_guidance: Investigate and revert if unauthorized.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1499.001: OS Exhaustion Flood

author: Threat Detection Library

title: DHCP Reservation Created
description: A new DHCP reservation binding a MAC/client identifier to a specific IP was created. Routine for infrastructure onboarding; the building block for the higher-priority reservation-abuse detections below.

data_sources.name: DHCP Audit Log
data_sources.description: Reservation creation events.

detection_logic: Filters reservation-creation events.
spl:
index=<dhcp_index> action="reservation created"
| table _time, host, user, scope, reservation_ip, reservation_mac
tuning_guidance: Not independently alertable at scale; feed into DHCP-026 through DHCP-030.
investigation_steps: Correlate with change management.
response_guidance: No independent response.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: DHCP Reservation MAC Address Changed
description: An existing reservation's MAC/client identifier was changed while the reserved IP stayed the same, meaning a new, different device will now receive that IP on its next DHCP request. If the reserved IP is trusted by firewall rules, NAC policy, or application allowlists keyed on IP, this silently reassigns that trust to a new device.

data_sources.name: DHCP Audit Log
data_sources.description: Reservation MAC-change events with old/new MAC.

detection_logic: Filters reservation-modification events where the MAC/client-identifier field changed.
spl:
index=<dhcp_index> action="reservation modified" field_changed="mac_address"
| table _time, host, user, scope, reservation_ip, old_mac, new_mac
tuning_guidance: Legitimate for hardware replacement (NIC swap); confirm against an asset-management ticket referencing the same device.
investigation_steps: Confirm the new MAC belongs to an approved device via asset inventory.
Check what trust (firewall/NAC/allowlist) is keyed on this IP.
response_guidance: Revert if unauthorized and audit any access the new device has already made using the reserved IP's trust.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: DHCP Reservation Reassigned from Legitimate to New MAC (Correlation)
description: A reservation's MAC changed and, within a short window, a device matching the new MAC actually leased the reserved (often privileged/trusted) IP — confirming the reassignment took effect and a new device is now operating with that IP's inherited trust.

data_sources.name: DHCP Audit Log
data_sources.description: Reservation MAC-change event followed by a lease event for the new MAC/IP pair.

detection_logic: Sequences a reservation MAC-change event with a subsequent lease event matching the new MAC/IP pair within a bounded window.
spl:
index=<dhcp_index> (action="reservation modified" field_changed="mac_address") OR action="lease"
| eval stage=case(action="reservation modified","1_reassign", action="lease","2_lease", true(), null())
| where isnotnull(stage)
| transaction reservation_ip maxspan=2h startswith=eval(stage="1_reassign") endswith=eval(stage="2_lease")
| table _time, reservation_ip, new_mac, eventcount
tuning_guidance: Correlate with the reservation-criticality lookup (privileged servers vs. general endpoints); escalate severity for reservations tied to trusted infrastructure.
investigation_steps: Treat as a confirmed device-swap; verify the new device's identity and legitimacy immediately.
Audit access performed using the reserved IP's inherited trust since the swap.
response_guidance: Revoke trust tied to the IP pending device verification; treat as a potential lateral-movement or trust-hijack incident.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Reservation Created for Privileged/Infrastructure Network Address
description: A new reservation was created targeting an IP address tagged as privileged infrastructure (e.g. within a management/identity/security-tooling range), which is worth extra scrutiny given the trust typically extended to such addresses.

data_sources.name: DHCP Audit Log
data_sources.description: Reservation creation events joined against a privileged-IP-range lookup.

detection_logic: Joins reservation-creation events against a lookup of privileged/infrastructure IP ranges.
spl:
index=<dhcp_index> action="reservation created"
| lookup privileged_ip_ranges.csv reservation_ip OUTPUT is_privileged
| where is_privileged=1
| table _time, host, user, reservation_ip, reservation_mac
tuning_guidance: Requires a maintained privileged-IP-range lookup.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification and the device's identity.
response_guidance: Remove if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Unusual Number of Reservations Created by Single Account
description: A single account created an unusually large number of reservations in a short window, which is atypical for routine per-device onboarding and more consistent with a scripted bulk operation.

data_sources.name: DHCP Audit Log
data_sources.description: Reservation creation count per account in a rolling window.

detection_logic: Counts reservation-creation events by the same account in a rolling window.
spl:
index=<dhcp_index> action="reservation created"
| bin _time span=1h
| stats count as reservations_created by _time user
| where reservations_created>=20
tuning_guidance: Tune out known bulk-onboarding automation accounts.
investigation_steps: Identify the account and confirm against known automation tooling.
response_guidance: Investigate if not attributable to approved tooling.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Duplicate or Conflicting Reservations Detected
description: Two reservations reference the same IP address with different MACs, or the same MAC with different IPs, which is an invalid/conflicting configuration that can cause unpredictable lease behavior and may indicate tampering rather than a simple misconfiguration.

data_sources.name: DHCP Audit Log
data_sources.description: Current reservation table checked for duplicate IP or MAC values.

detection_logic: Groups the current reservation set by IP and by MAC and flags any group with more than one distinct counterpart.
spl:
| inputlookup dhcp_current_reservations.csv
| stats dc(reservation_mac) as macs_per_ip, values(reservation_mac) as macs by reservation_ip
| where macs_per_ip>1
tuning_guidance: Requires a periodic reservation-table export; low volume once available.
investigation_steps: Determine which reservation is legitimate and remove the conflicting one.
response_guidance: Resolve the conflict and investigate how it was introduced.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Reservation Modified Outside Change Window
description: A reservation was modified outside any declared maintenance/change window.

data_sources.name: DHCP Audit Log
data_sources.description: Reservation modification events joined against a maintenance calendar.

detection_logic: Filters reservation-modification events where a maintenance-window lookup does not cover the event time.
spl:
index=<dhcp_index> action="reservation modified"
| lookup maintenance_windows.csv host, _time OUTPUT in_window
| where isnull(in_window) OR in_window=0
| table _time, host, user, reservation_ip
tuning_guidance: Requires a maintained maintenance-window lookup; expect a higher false-positive rate without one.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification.
response_guidance: Low urgency alone; escalate if correlated with DHCP-026/027.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: DHCP Reservation Deleted
description: A reservation was deleted, releasing its IP back to the general leasable pool where any client can obtain it — potentially removing intended device-to-address binding for an infrastructure system.

data_sources.name: DHCP Audit Log
data_sources.description: Reservation deletion events.

detection_logic: Filters reservation-deletion events.
spl:
index=<dhcp_index> action="reservation deleted"
| table _time, host, user, reservation_ip, reservation_mac
tuning_guidance: Confirm against decommission tickets.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification.
Monitor the released IP for the next lease issued.
response_guidance: Recreate if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: DHCP DNS Server Option (006) Changed
description: Option 006 (DNS Servers) was changed on a scope or at the server level. Since every client that renews its lease will start using the new DNS server(s), this can redirect DNS resolution for large numbers of endpoints without touching any of them directly — a foundational technique for DNS hijacking, phishing infrastructure redirection, and credential capture via lookalike resolution.

data_sources.name: DHCP Audit Log
data_sources.description: Option value-change events for option 006.

detection_logic: Filters DHCP option-change events for option 006 and compares the new value against the approved DNS server allowlist.
spl:
index=<dhcp_index> action="option value set" option_id=6
| lookup approved_dns_servers.csv new_value AS server OUTPUT is_approved
| where isnull(is_approved)
| table _time, host, user, scope, old_value, new_value
tuning_guidance: Maintain the approved-DNS-server allowlist; alert on every value not on it.
investigation_steps: Treat as a live incident.
Identify every client that has renewed a lease since the change.
Verify the new DNS server(s) are not attacker-controlled.
response_guidance: Revert immediately and force-renew affected clients; treat any client that resolved through the rogue DNS server as potentially exposed to malicious responses.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: DHCP DNS Server Option Changed Across Multiple Scopes
description: The same new DNS server value was pushed to option 006 across many scopes in a short window, indicating a fleet-wide DNS redirection rather than a single-scope change — dramatically larger blast radius.

data_sources.name: DHCP Audit Log
data_sources.description: Option 006 change events grouped by new value across scopes.

detection_logic: Groups option 006 change events by new value and counts distinct scopes affected in a rolling window.
spl:
index=<dhcp_index> action="option value set" option_id=6
| bin _time span=1h
| stats dc(scope) as scopes_affected by new_value, user, _time
| where scopes_affected>=3
tuning_guidance: Very low expected false-positive rate; treat as a fleet-wide incident.
investigation_steps: Treat as a fleet-wide incident.
Identify every affected scope and client population.
response_guidance: Full incident response across every affected scope.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: DHCP Domain Name Option (015) or Domain Search List (119) Changed
description: Option 015 (DNS Domain Name) or option 119 (Domain Search List) was changed, altering how clients resolve unqualified hostnames — an attacker-controlled search suffix can cause internal short-name lookups (e.g. \\fileserver) to silently resolve against an attacker-controlled domain instead.

data_sources.name: DHCP Audit Log
data_sources.description: Option value-change events for options 015 and 119.

detection_logic: Filters DHCP option-change events for options 015/119.
spl:
index=<dhcp_index> action="option value set" option_id IN (15,119)
| table _time, host, user, scope, option_id, old_value, new_value
tuning_guidance: Very low expected volume outside domain restructuring; alert on all occurrences.
investigation_steps: Verify the new domain/search suffix is legitimately owned by the organization.
response_guidance: Revert immediately if unrecognized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: DHCP DNS Server Option Order Changed
description: The order of servers listed in the DNS server option was changed without adding/removing a server, which can promote a secondary/attacker-influenced resolver to primary position where it will be queried first.

data_sources.name: DHCP Audit Log
data_sources.description: Option 006 value-change events where the same set of servers is reordered.

detection_logic: Compares old and new option 006 values as sets; flags events where the set is unchanged but the order differs.
spl:
index=<dhcp_index> action="option value set" option_id=6
| eval old_sorted=mvjoin(sort(split(old_value,",")),",")
| eval new_sorted=mvjoin(sort(split(new_value,",")),",")
| where old_sorted=new_sorted AND old_value!=new_value
| table _time, host, user, scope, old_value, new_value
tuning_guidance: Low volume; alert on all occurrences.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification for the reorder.
response_guidance: Revert if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: DHCP Default Gateway Option (003) Changed
description: Option 003 (Router/Default Gateway) was changed on a scope or at the server level. Clients that renew will begin routing all off-subnet traffic through the new gateway — a foundational technique for man-in-the-middle interception, traffic capture, and network pivoting without touching any endpoint directly.

data_sources.name: DHCP Audit Log
data_sources.description: Option value-change events for option 003.

detection_logic: Filters DHCP option-change events for option 003 and compares the new value against the approved gateway allowlist per subnet.
spl:
index=<dhcp_index> action="option value set" option_id=3
| lookup approved_gateways.csv scope, new_value AS gateway OUTPUT is_approved
| where isnull(is_approved)
| table _time, host, user, scope, old_value, new_value
tuning_guidance: Maintain the approved-gateway-per-subnet allowlist; alert on every value not on it.
investigation_steps: Treat as a live incident.
Verify the new gateway address is a legitimate network device, not an endpoint-class address.
response_guidance: Revert immediately; treat all traffic that traversed the rogue gateway as potentially intercepted.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: DHCP Gateway Changed to Endpoint-Class Address
description: The new gateway address falls within the scope's own leasable client-address range rather than the expected router/infrastructure address, strongly suggesting an attacker is directing traffic through a compromised or attacker-controlled endpoint acting as a rogue gateway.

data_sources.name: DHCP Audit Log
data_sources.description: Option 003 changes where the new value falls inside the scope's own lease range.

detection_logic: Compares the new option 003 value against the scope's own start/end lease range.
spl:
index=<dhcp_index> action="option value set" option_id=3
| eval in_client_range=if(new_value>=scope_start AND new_value<=scope_end, 1, 0)
| where in_client_range=1
| table _time, host, user, scope, new_value
tuning_guidance: Extremely low expected false-positive rate; alert on every occurrence.
investigation_steps: Treat as a confirmed man-in-the-middle setup.
Identify the device now operating at the new gateway address.
response_guidance: Revert immediately and isolate the device at the rogue gateway address.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Same New Gateway Pushed Across Multiple Scopes
description: The same new gateway value was pushed to option 003 across multiple scopes in a short window, indicating a fleet-wide traffic-redirection attempt.

data_sources.name: DHCP Audit Log
data_sources.description: Option 003 change events grouped by new value across scopes.

detection_logic: Groups option 003 change events by new value and counts distinct scopes affected in a rolling window.
spl:
index=<dhcp_index> action="option value set" option_id=3
| bin _time span=1h
| stats dc(scope) as scopes_affected by new_value, user, _time
| where scopes_affected>=3
tuning_guidance: Very low expected false-positive rate; treat as a fleet-wide incident.
investigation_steps: Treat as a fleet-wide incident.
response_guidance: Full incident response across every affected scope.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: DHCP Classless Static Route Option (121/249) Created or Modified
description: Option 121 (Classless Static Routes) or 249 (Microsoft Classless Static Routes) was created or modified, injecting a static route into every client that receives it — without touching the client's own routing configuration. This can silently divert traffic destined for a specific network (e.g. identity, security-tooling, or backup infrastructure) through an attacker-controlled next-hop while leaving all other traffic unaffected and less likely to be noticed than a full gateway change.

data_sources.name: DHCP Audit Log
data_sources.description: Option value-change events for options 121/249.

detection_logic: Filters DHCP option-change events for options 121/249.
spl:
index=<dhcp_index> action="option value set" option_id IN (121,249)
| table _time, host, user, scope, option_id, old_value, new_value
tuning_guidance: Very low expected volume outside planned routing changes; alert on all occurrences.
investigation_steps: Treat as a live incident.
Decode the destination network and next-hop from the option value and verify both are legitimate.
response_guidance: Revert immediately if unrecognized; treat traffic to the affected destination network as potentially intercepted since the change.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: DHCP Static Route Targets Identity or Security Infrastructure
description: A new static route option's destination network overlaps with a subnet tagged as identity (AD/IdP), security-tooling (SIEM/EDR management), or backup infrastructure, meaning traffic to that specific high-value network could be redirected through an attacker-controlled next-hop.

data_sources.name: DHCP Audit Log
data_sources.description: Option 121/249 changes joined against a sensitive-subnet lookup.

detection_logic: Decodes the destination network from options 121/249 and joins against a sensitive-subnet lookup.
spl:
index=<dhcp_index> action="option value set" option_id IN (121,249)
| lookup sensitive_subnets.csv destination_network OUTPUT subnet_tag
| where isnotnull(subnet_tag)
| table _time, host, user, scope, destination_network, subnet_tag
tuning_guidance: Requires a maintained sensitive-subnet lookup; extremely high value once available.
investigation_steps: Treat as a live incident given the destination sensitivity.
response_guidance: Revert immediately.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: New Default Route Injected via DHCP Static Route Option
description: A static route option was set with a 0.0.0.0/0 destination, which functions as an alternative default route independent of option 003, and can be used to redirect all traffic even if the standard gateway option looks unchanged.

data_sources.name: DHCP Audit Log
data_sources.description: Option 121/249 changes where the decoded destination is 0.0.0.0/0.

detection_logic: Decodes the destination network from options 121/249 and flags a 0.0.0.0/0 destination.
spl:
index=<dhcp_index> action="option value set" option_id IN (121,249)
| where destination_network="0.0.0.0/0"
| table _time, host, user, scope, next_hop
tuning_guidance: Very low expected volume; alert on all occurrences.
investigation_steps: Treat as equivalent in severity to DHCP-033/034.
response_guidance: Revert immediately.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: DHCP Static Route Option Deleted
description: A previously configured static route option was removed, which can break intentional network segmentation/routing designs that depended on it (e.g. routing to a specific security-tooling segment).

data_sources.name: DHCP Audit Log
data_sources.description: Option 121/249 deletion events.

detection_logic: Filters option-deletion events for options 121/249.
spl:
index=<dhcp_index> action="option deleted" option_id IN (121,249)
| table _time, host, user, scope
tuning_guidance: Confirm against change tickets.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification and assess routing impact.
response_guidance: Restore if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: DHCP PXE Boot Server Option (066) Changed
description: Option 066 (Boot Server Host Name) was changed, redirecting PXE-booting clients to a different TFTP/boot server. Since PXE boot happens before the client OS loads, a client pointed at an attacker-controlled boot server can be handed a malicious pre-OS image — one of the most severe possible DHCP-mediated compromises.

data_sources.name: DHCP Audit Log
data_sources.description: Option 066 value-change events.

detection_logic: Filters option-change events for option 066 and compares the new value against the approved PXE/boot infrastructure allowlist.
spl:
index=<dhcp_index> action="option value set" option_id=66
| lookup approved_pxe_servers.csv new_value AS server OUTPUT is_approved
| where isnull(is_approved)
| table _time, host, user, scope, old_value, new_value
tuning_guidance: Maintain the approved-PXE-server allowlist; alert on every value not on it.
investigation_steps: Treat as a live incident.
Identify every client that has PXE-booted since the change.
response_guidance: Revert immediately; treat any client that PXE-booted through the rogue server as potentially compromised at the pre-OS level, warranting a full rebuild.
author: Threat Detection Library
attack_mapping_note: ATT&CK T1542 (Pre-OS Boot) is the closest-fit technique for PXE boot-server redirection via DHCP; it is used despite the compromise happening through the network boot path rather than direct on-host firmware tampering, because the resulting effect (attacker controls what boots) is functionally equivalent.

title: DHCP PXE Boot Filename Option (067) Changed
description: Option 067 (Bootfile Name) was changed, altering which boot loader/image file PXE clients request from the boot server — the second half of the PXE compromise chain alongside DHCP-040.

data_sources.name: DHCP Audit Log
data_sources.description: Option 067 value-change events.

detection_logic: Filters option-change events for option 067.
spl:
index=<dhcp_index> action="option value set" option_id=67
| table _time, host, user, scope, old_value, new_value
tuning_guidance: Very low expected volume outside planned imaging infrastructure changes; alert on all occurrences.
investigation_steps: Verify the boot file is the expected, unmodified image.
response_guidance: Revert immediately if unrecognized.
author: Threat Detection Library
attack_mapping_note: ATT&CK T1542 (Pre-OS Boot) used as closest-fit for the same reason as DHCP-040.

title: DHCP Vendor Class Identifier Option (060) Changed
description: Option 060 (Vendor Class Identifier), commonly used to identify and route PXE clients, was changed, which can affect which policy or boot configuration a class of devices receives.

data_sources.name: DHCP Audit Log
data_sources.description: Option 060 value-change events.

detection_logic: Filters option-change events for option 060.
spl:
index=<dhcp_index> action="option value set" option_id=60
| table _time, host, user, scope, old_value, new_value
tuning_guidance: Confirm against imaging-infrastructure change tickets.
investigation_steps: Verify the new vendor class value is expected.
response_guidance: Revert if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library
attack_mapping_note: ATT&CK T1542 (Pre-OS Boot) used as closest-fit; a vendor-class change alone is a lower-confidence precursor than DHCP-040/041.

title: PXE Configuration Pushed to New Scopes
description: PXE-related options (060/066/067) were configured on scopes that did not previously have them, expanding the set of network segments where clients can be redirected to a boot server — worth scrutiny if that expansion touches segments that should never PXE boot (e.g. server VLANs, guest networks).

data_sources.name: DHCP Audit Log
data_sources.description: First-seen PXE option configuration per scope.

detection_logic: Compares scopes with newly-set PXE options against a baseline of scopes previously known to have PXE configured.
spl:
index=<dhcp_index> action="option value set" option_id IN (60,66,67)
| lookup pxe_enabled_scopes_baseline.csv scope OUTPUT was_pxe_enabled
| where isnull(was_pxe_enabled)
| table _time, host, user, scope, option_id
tuning_guidance: Requires a maintained baseline of scopes expected to support PXE; expected during planned imaging-infrastructure expansion.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification.
Verify the newly-PXE-enabled scope's role (should not be a server/guest VLAN).
response_guidance: Remove if unauthorized, especially on inappropriate network segments.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: PXE Boot Followed by Client Network Boot Activity
description: A DHCP PXE option change (DHCP-040/041) is immediately followed by a client actually requesting the boot server/file via network telemetry (TFTP request), confirming the compromised path was exercised by a real client and not just configured.

data_sources.name: DHCP audit log + network telemetry (Zeek/Suricata TFTP)
data_sources.path: PXE option change joined with subsequent TFTP GET requests to the same boot server
data_sources.description: Requires network-level TFTP visibility.

detection_logic: Sequences a PXE option-change event with a subsequent TFTP request to the new boot server within a bounded window.
spl:
(index=<dhcp_index> action="option value set" option_id IN (66,67))
OR (index=<network_index> sourcetype=<tftp_sourcetype> action="GET")
| eval stage=case(action="option value set","1_config", action="GET","2_tftp_fetch", true(), null())
| where isnotnull(stage)
| transaction boot_server maxspan=1h startswith=eval(stage="1_config") endswith=eval(stage="2_tftp_fetch")
| table _time, boot_server, eventcount
tuning_guidance: Requires network-level TFTP visibility (Zeek/Suricata); this library does not claim Windows DHCP logs alone provide this correlation.
investigation_steps: Identify the client that fetched the boot image and treat it as compromised at the pre-OS level.
response_guidance: Isolate and rebuild the affected client(s) from known-good media.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: DHCP Policy Created
description: A new DHCP policy was created. Policies can conditionally assign different options (including DNS/gateway) based on MAC prefix, vendor class, or user class, making them an alternative, less-obvious path to the same DNS/gateway-redirection outcomes covered above.

data_sources.name: DHCP Audit Log
data_sources.description: Policy creation events.

detection_logic: Filters policy-creation events.
spl:
index=<dhcp_index> action="policy created"
| table _time, host, user, policy, conditions
tuning_guidance: Confirm against change tickets; low volume in most environments.
investigation_steps: Review the policy's conditions and assigned options for anything matching DHCP-DNS-###/DHCP-033-###-style redirection.
response_guidance: Remove if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: DHCP Policy Assigns DNS/Gateway Options Differing from Scope Default
description: A DHCP policy assigns a DNS server or gateway option value that differs from the scope's own default, meaning only clients matching the policy's condition (e.g. a specific MAC prefix or vendor class) receive the redirected value — a targeted, harder-to-notice variant of DHCP-DNS-001/DHCP-033 that evades detections scoped only to the default scope options.

data_sources.name: DHCP Audit Log
data_sources.description: Policy option assignments compared against the parent scope's default option values.

detection_logic: Compares each policy's assigned option 003/006 value against its parent scope's default value.
spl:
index=<dhcp_index> action="policy option set" option_id IN (3,6)
| lookup scope_default_options.csv scope, option_id OUTPUT scope_default_value
| where policy_value!=scope_default_value
| table _time, host, user, policy, option_id, policy_value, scope_default_value
tuning_guidance: Requires maintaining a scope-default-options lookup; very high value given how targeted this attack path is.
investigation_steps: Identify exactly which devices match the policy condition and are therefore being redirected.
Treat with the same urgency as DHCP-DNS-001/DHCP-033.
response_guidance: Remove/revert the policy immediately if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: DHCP Policy Targets Specific MAC Prefix or Vendor Class
description: A DHCP policy's matching condition is scoped to a narrow MAC OUI prefix or specific vendor class rather than a broad device population, which — combined with option-assignment scrutiny (DHCP-046) — is consistent with an attacker crafting a policy to target only a specific class of device (e.g. a particular vendor's servers or security appliances) rather than the whole network, minimizing detection.

data_sources.name: DHCP Audit Log
data_sources.description: Policy condition configuration.

detection_logic: Filters policy configuration events where the condition type is a MAC prefix or vendor class match.
spl:
index=<dhcp_index> action="policy created" OR action="policy condition changed"
| where condition_type IN ("mac_prefix","vendor_class")
| table _time, host, user, policy, condition_type, condition_value
tuning_guidance: Not independently critical; cross-reference against DHCP-046 for option assignment before escalating.
investigation_steps: Determine which real devices the condition matches.
response_guidance: Review in conjunction with the policy's assigned options.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: DHCP Policy Processing Order Changed
description: The processing order of DHCP policies was changed, which determines which policy's option assignments take precedence when multiple policies match the same client — reordering can silently promote a malicious policy above a legitimate one.

data_sources.name: DHCP Audit Log
data_sources.description: Policy processing-order configuration change events.

detection_logic: Filters policy processing-order change events.
spl:
index=<dhcp_index> action="policy order changed"
| table _time, host, user, scope, new_order
tuning_guidance: Confirm against change tickets.
investigation_steps: Review the resulting effective policy order for any suspicious policy being promoted.
response_guidance: Revert if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: DHCP Policy Enabled or Disabled
description: A DHCP policy's enabled/disabled state was toggled, which activates or deactivates its conditional option assignments.

data_sources.name: DHCP Audit Log
data_sources.description: Policy state-change events.

detection_logic: Filters policy enable/disable events.
spl:
index=<dhcp_index> action="policy state changed"
| table _time, host, user, policy, new_state
tuning_guidance: Not independently high value; correlate with DHCP-046 to assess whether the toggled policy is redirection-capable.
investigation_steps: Review the policy's option assignments if newly enabled.
response_guidance: Investigate if newly enabled and unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: DHCP Allow/Deny Filter List Changed
description: The MAC-address allow or deny filter list was modified, which controls which client MACs are permitted or blocked from receiving a lease regardless of scope configuration.

data_sources.name: DHCP Audit Log
data_sources.description: Filter list modification events.

detection_logic: Filters filter-list modification events.
spl:
index=<dhcp_index> action="filter list changed"
| table _time, host, user, filter_list, mac_address, filter_action
tuning_guidance: Confirm against change tickets; low volume in most environments.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification for the specific MAC(s) added/removed.
response_guidance: Revert if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Large Batch of MACs Added to DHCP Filter List
description: An unusually large number of MAC addresses were added to a filter list in a short window, which could deny a large population of legitimate devices (if added to a deny list) or grant broad rogue access (if added to an allow list).

data_sources.name: DHCP Audit Log
data_sources.description: Filter list additions counted in a rolling window.

detection_logic: Counts filter-list addition events in a rolling window.
spl:
index=<dhcp_index> action="filter list changed" filter_action="added"
| bin _time span=1h
| stats count as macs_added by _time user filter_list
| where macs_added>=20
tuning_guidance: Confirm against bulk-onboarding change tickets.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification for the bulk addition.
response_guidance: Investigate and revert if unauthorized.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1499.001: OS Exhaustion Flood

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Known Infrastructure MAC Added to Deny Filter
description: A MAC address belonging to known infrastructure (per an asset inventory) was added to the deny filter list, which will prevent that device from obtaining or renewing a lease — a targeted denial-of-service against a specific system.

data_sources.name: DHCP Audit Log
data_sources.description: Deny-filter additions joined against an asset-inventory lookup.

detection_logic: Joins deny-filter addition events against an asset-inventory lookup and flags matches.
spl:
index=<dhcp_index> action="filter list changed" filter_list="deny" filter_action="added"
| lookup asset_inventory.csv mac_address OUTPUT asset_name, asset_criticality
| where isnotnull(asset_name)
| table _time, host, user, mac_address, asset_name, asset_criticality
tuning_guidance: Requires a maintained asset-inventory lookup; alert on all matches.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification for denying this specific device
response_guidance: Remove from the deny list immediately if unauthorized.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1499.001: OS Exhaustion Flood

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Unknown/Attacker MAC Explicitly Added to Allow Filter
description: A MAC address not present in the asset inventory was added to the allow filter list, which — in an environment where the allow list is the sole gate on which devices may lease addresses — grants network access to an unrecognized device.

data_sources.name: DHCP Audit Log
data_sources.description: Allow-filter additions joined against an asset-inventory lookup.

detection_logic: Joins allow-filter addition events against an asset-inventory lookup and flags misses.
spl:
index=<dhcp_index> action="filter list changed" filter_list="allow" filter_action="added"
| lookup asset_inventory.csv mac_address OUTPUT asset_name
| where isnull(asset_name)
| table _time, host, user, mac_address
tuning_guidance: Requires a maintained asset-inventory lookup and only applies where allow-list filtering is the network access control model.
investigation_steps: Identify the device behind the MAC before it obtains a lease.
response_guidance: Remove from the allow list pending device identification.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1499.001: OS Exhaustion Flood

author: Threat Detection Library

title: DHCP Failover Relationship Created
description: A new DHCP failover relationship was created between two servers, establishing lease-state replication and shared responsibility for a scope.

data_sources.name: DHCP Audit Log
data_sources.description: Failover relationship creation events.

detection_logic: Filters failover relationship creation events.
spl:
index=<dhcp_index> action="failover relationship created"
| table _time, host, user, partner_server
tuning_guidance: Confirm against change tickets for planned HA deployment.
investigation_steps: Verify the partner server is a legitimate, expected DHCP server.
response_guidance: Remove if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: DHCP Failover Partner Changed
description: An existing failover relationship's partner server was changed to a different server, which will begin replicating lease state to (and sharing serving responsibility with) a new server — if that new server is attacker-controlled, it gains authoritative visibility into and influence over lease issuance for the shared scope.

data_sources.name: DHCP Audit Log
data_sources.description: Failover partner-change events with old/new partner.

detection_logic: Filters failover relationship configuration change events for the partner field.
spl:
index=<dhcp_index> action="failover relationship modified" field_changed="partner_server"
